targets.authors: Grosjean, P., Masera, F. and Yousaf, H.
targets.title: Inflammatory political campaigns and racial bias in policing
targets.evidence_quote:
Grosjean et al. (2023) (GMY2023) estimate the causal effect of a Trump
      rally on the number of black drivers stopped by police officers, using a diffence-
      in-difference approach. In their preferred specification, the authors find that
      after a Trump rally, the probability that a stopped driver is black increases
      by 5.74 %. This effect is significant at the 1 % level. In this report we
      focus on reproducing the main claim of the paper.
targets.outcome_computational_quote:
First, we reproduce the
      paper’s main findings and uncover an issue with counties that experience
      multiple Trump rally treatments, given the original modelling choices taken
      in GMY2023.
targets.outcome_robustness_quote:
We find that the results
are driven by counties with repeat rallies. Once we exclude these counties, the
results disappear.

reasoning: The main exercise reproduces original findings and changes specifications on original data. Both reproduction axes are explicit. The report also includes a new-source NIBRS replication; this additional exercise is not used to determine robustness of the original data. Single record type follows the primary original-data reanalysis. PDF title matches the assigned descriptive author field; no report authors are printed.
